newsitem.title: USA: Investor says to sue Business Week for libel.
newsitem.headline: Investor says to sue Business Week for libel.

text.p: Hedge fund investor Julian Robertson has filed notice he plans to sue Business Week for libel over an article the magazine wrote about him last year, his spokesman said Friday.

The article, called "Fall of the Wizard" ran in the McGraw-Hill Cos Inc publication in its April 1, 1996 edition. It examined the performance of Robertson's Tiger Management Corp, which he founded in 1980.
It detailed what Business Week called "the story of a man who rose to greatness -- only to be foiled by his own overcontrolling management style and hot temper."

Fraser Seitel, a spokesman for Robertson, said a notice was filed in New York Supreme Court indicating Robertson's intention to sue Business Week. The lawsuit is to allege the article contained "false and defamatory statements," Seitel said.
Seitel said Robertson would not immediately disclose, which statements he believed were libelous.
A spokesman for Business Week did not immediately return a telephone call.
"We have not yet been served and, therefore, we have nothing to respond to," Neal Allen, a spokesman for McGraw-Hill, said later Friday.
